name: Question 7
problem:
Find the general solution to the  equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+4y=8\operatorname{cos}⁡2x-\operatorname{sin}⁡2x.
$$
worked_solution:
First, we need to find the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x),$ which is the solution to the homogeneous equation

$$
\frac{{\text{d}}^{2}y}{\text{d}{x}^{2}}+4y=0.
$$

Writing down and solving the auxiliary equation gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}+4 & =0 \\ {\lambda }^{2} & =-4\end{aligned}
$$

So $\lambda =\pm \text{2i}$, and therefore the complementary function ${y}_{c}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{c}=P\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡2x.
$$

We now need to find the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x).$ 

The particular solution of the inhomogeneous equation cannot be of the form $\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡2x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡2x$ because this is already included in the complementary function. Therefore, we assume a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}=x(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡2x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡2x),
$$

where $\alpha $ and $\beta $ are constants that are to be determined. 

Calculating the first and second derivatives of ${y}_{p}$ gives:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}x} & =(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡2x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡2x)+2x(-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡2x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡2x) \\ \frac{{\text{d}}^{2}{y}_{p}}{\text{d}{x}^{2}} & =4(-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡2x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡2x)-4x(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡2x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡2x)\end{aligned}
$$

To find the values of $\alpha $ and $\beta ,$ we substitute the derivatives into the differential equation:

$$
4(-\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡2x+\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡2x)-4x(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡2x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡2x)+4x(\alpha \operatorname{cos}⁡2x+\beta \operatorname{sin}⁡2x)=8\operatorname{cos}⁡2x-\operatorname{sin}⁡2x
$$

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives

$$
-4\alpha \operatorname{sin}⁡2x+4\beta \operatorname{cos}⁡2x=8\operatorname{cos}⁡2x-\operatorname{sin}⁡2x.
$$

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\begin{aligned}4\beta =8\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{cos}⁡2x) \\ -4\alpha =-1\, & (\text{equating the coefficients of}\,\operatorname{sin}⁡2x)\end{aligned}\end{aligned}
$$

Solving this system gives $\alpha =\frac{1}{4}$ and $\beta =2.$

Therefore, the particular solution ${y}_{p}(x)$ is

$$
{y}_{p}(x)=x(\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+2\operatorname{sin}⁡2x).
$$

The general solution is given by

$$
y(x)={y}_{c}(x)+{y}_{p}(x),
$$

and therefore, the general solution in our case is

$$
y=P\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+Q\operatorname{sin}⁡2x+x(\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{cos}⁡2x+2\operatorname{sin}⁡2x).
$$

Question 7

Find the general solution to the equation d2ydx2+4y=8cos⁡2x−sin⁡2x.

a
y=Pcos⁡2x+Qsin⁡2x+x(32cos⁡2x−sin⁡2x)
b
y=Pcos⁡x+Qsin⁡x+14cos⁡2x+12sin⁡2x
c
y=Pcos⁡2x+Qsin⁡2x+x(34cos⁡2x+sin⁡2x)
d
y=Pcos⁡2x+Qsin⁡2x+x(14cos⁡2x+2sin⁡2x)
e
y=Pcos⁡x+Qsin⁡x+cos⁡2x−12sin⁡2x
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

First, we need to find the complementary function yc(x), which is the solution to the homogeneous equation d2ydx2+4y=0.

Writing down and solving the auxiliary equation gives: λ2+4=0λ2=−4

So λ=±2i, and therefore the complementary function yc(x) is yc=Pcos⁡2x+Qsin⁡2x.

We now need to find the particular solution yp(x).

The particular solution of the inhomogeneous equation cannot be of the form αcos⁡2x+βsin⁡2x because this is already included in the complementary function. Therefore, we assume a particular solution of the form yp=x(αcos⁡2x+βsin⁡2x), where α and β are constants that are to be determined.

Calculating the first and second derivatives of yp gives: dypdx=(αcos⁡2x+βsin⁡2x)+2x(−αsin⁡2x+βcos⁡2x)d2ypdx2=4(−αsin⁡2x+βcos⁡2x)−4x(αcos⁡2x+βsin⁡2x)

To find the values of α and β, we substitute the derivatives into the differential equation: 4(−αsin⁡2x+βcos⁡2x)−4x(αcos⁡2x+βsin⁡2x)+4x(αcos⁡2x+βsin⁡2x)=8cos⁡2x−sin⁡2x

Grouping the terms on the left-hand side gives −4αsin⁡2x+4βcos⁡2x=8cos⁡2x−sin⁡2x.

Equating the coefficients, we get the following system of equations: {4β=8(equating the coefficients ofcos⁡2x)−4α=−1(equating the coefficients ofsin⁡2x)

Solving this system gives α=14 and β=2.

Therefore, the particular solution yp(x) is yp(x)=x(14cos⁡2x+2sin⁡2x).

The general solution is given by y(x)=yc(x)+yp(x), and therefore, the general solution in our case is y=Pcos⁡2x+Qsin⁡2x+x(14cos⁡2x+2sin⁡2x).
